items.term: who / that for people (the woman who called)
items.es: who o that para personas: la mujer que llamó

example.en: The woman who called you is my aunt.
example.es: La mujer que te llamó es mi tía.

items.term: which / that for things (the bus that goes downtown)
items.es: which o that para cosas: el autobús que va al centro

example.en: I lost the book that you gave me.
example.es: Perdí el libro que me diste.

items.term: where for places (the town where I grew up)
items.es: where para lugares: el pueblo donde crecí

example.en: This is the street where I grew up.
example.es: Esta es la calle donde crecí.

example.en: I have a friend whose mother is a doctor.
example.es: Tengo un amigo cuya mamá es médica.

items.term: relative clause without who / that (the movie we saw)
items.es: oración de relativo sin who ni that: la película que vimos

example.en: The movie we saw last night was great.
example.es: La película que vimos anoche fue excelente.

items.term: extra information between commas (my sister, who lives in Miami, …)
items.es: información extra entre comas: mi hermana, que vive en Miami, …

example.en: My sister, who lives in Miami, is a nurse.
example.es: Mi hermana, que vive en Miami, es enfermera.

passages.title: My new neighborhood
passages.text: Last month I moved to a small apartment in a neighborhood where everyone seems to know each other. The woman who lives across the hall is a retired teacher, and she has already invited me for coffee twice. Downstairs there is a bakery that sells the best bread in town. The owner, whose family is from Italy, gets up at four every morning. There is also a park where kids play soccer after school. The only thing I don't like is the bus that goes to my office: it's always late!
